newsitem.title: USA: S.F. 49ers may leave city if stadium fails - paper.
newsitem.headline: S.F. 49ers may leave city if stadium fails - paper.

text.p: The 49ers would leave San Francisco in 2006 if the team's football stadium proposal fails in June, team president Carmen Policy told the San Francisco Chronicle, the newspaper reported Tuesday.
"If we don't have a place to play in San Francisco, what can we do? Candlestick Park is not suitable for National Football League play after 2006," Policy told the Chronicle.
If the 49ers do not get a majority vote in the city's June 3 special election, Policy said, "It will be the community kicking us out. We're being escorted out of town."
The 49ers project is projected to cost about $537 million, including $250 million for a proposed stadium and $200 million for the proposed entertainment and shopping complex.
To help finance the project, city officials have proposed a $100 million lease-revenue bond issue that would be placed on the June 3 ballot, city officials said.
